solver.method: binary search against the final deformed anatomical fin metric after pairing mirrored sheets
solver.reason: Raw connected components are surface sheets, not necessarily separate anatomical fins. The first run also proved that target/current scaling is invalid under root pinning and smoothstep attenuation.

bodyPolicy.caudalFade: zero body-depth correction at and behind the inferred fork
bodyPolicy.headFade: return smoothly to the frozen snout

finPolicy.pectoral: extend each connected side-fin component away from its shared body root; root vertices remain pinned
finPolicy.secondDorsal: extend both mirrored sheets of the second dorsal anatomical group, frozen components 2 and 4, with identical final height; root vertices remain pinned
finPolicy.anal: extend only the connected anal component with the greatest ventral height; root vertices remain pinned
finPolicy.firstDorsal: retain both mirrored sheets, frozen components 0 and 3, without independent elongation in Candidate A
finPolicy.posteriorDorsalStructure: do not relabel or independently rescale frozen component 1 in Candidate A
finPolicy.caudal: do not independently rescale in Candidate A
finPolicy.finlets: do not change counts or independently rescale in Candidate A
